title: Adaptive Scheduler 1.0 - Launch Notes and Operational Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page documents the 1.0 launch of the Adaptive Scheduler, a runtime-level scheduling engine that replaces the legacy static slot allocator for production workloads. The Adaptive Scheduler is intended to improve tail latency, reduce per-token cost via smarter slot consolidation, and provide fine-grained SLO-aware admission controls. This document summarizes architecture changes, kernel scheduling behavior, profiling and benchmark results, rollout and validation steps, operational runbooks, known issues discovered during canary, and rollback criteria.

Audience:
- Serving runtime engineers
- SREs and oncall defenders
- Runtime QA and benchmarking teams
- Product owners for Dedicated/Private customers with scheduler tunables

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- What: Adaptive Scheduler 1.0 introduces: predictive slot consolidation, per-request credit accounting, and SLO-driven admission policies.
- Why: Reduce tail 95/99 latency by 20–40% on mixed workloads and reduce unit GPU time for low-latency small requests by ~8% in our benchmarks.
- Risk: Medium — changes to admission and kernel handoff behavior can influence eviction patterns and KV cache locality.
- Rollout: Canary -> graduated regional rollout -> global by-service rollout. Follow the Validation checklist below.

Key changes (high level):
1) Scheduler behavior
   - Predictive consolidation: uses a short lookback of sequence-length histograms + model variant hints to coalesce compatible requests into shared slots where latency SLOs permit.
   - Credit accounting: per-tenant credit buckets to reduce noisy-neighbor effects; credits replenish at configurable rates.
   - Priority synthesis: combines customer route priority, inferred latency sensitivity, and experiment flags to produce an execution priority score used during contention.

2) Kernel handoff and prefetch
   - Lazy kernel hedging when predicted queueing > 120ms (config flag). This triggers speculative kernel activation for long sequences to avoid warmstart hit.
   - Prefetch hints are emitted to the KV cache manager for requests expected to exceed 64 tokens.

3) Observability and control surface
   - New telemetry metrics: scheduler.priority_score, scheduler.slot_coalesce_ratio, scheduler.credit_usage, scheduler.speculative_kernels.
   - New control knobs (runtime-config API): consolidation_enabled (bool), credit_window_ms (int), speculative_hedge_threshold_ms (int), coalesce_allowed_models (list).

Runtime architecture impact (detailed):
- Placement: The scheduler acts as a thin service in the request path prior to the kernel dispatcher. It remains colocated on dispatcher nodes to preserve per-request provenance.
- Stateful components: lightweight time-series lookback buffer (per-node, in-memory, ring-buffer); credit buckets persisted to the local faststore with periodic snapshots to the control plane for global accounting.
- Failure modes: if the scheduler process crashes we fall back to the static allocator (fallback_adapter). The fallback path is implemented with the same admission checks but without consolidation.

Kernel scheduling and compatibility notes:
- Kernel hinting: the scheduler may select a kernel variant with lower memory overhead but slightly higher compute latency if coalescing yields a net latency improvement for the cohort.
- Eviction interplay: speculative hedging increases temporary KV cache churn; the eviction policy has been retuned to raise kvcache.eviction_threshold from 0.65 -> 0.72 during canary. Monitor kvcache.hit_rate and pagefaults.

Profiling playbook updates (what to run and where to look):
- Baseline captures: run a 60-minute shadow capture of representative mixed traffic (small chat + long generation + embedding spikes) using the profiling harness.
- Traces to collect: full span traces with scheduler.priority_score tag, kernel variant IDs, kvcache.hint tags, and per-token timing.
- Sampling guidance: during canary set sample_rate_inbound_traces to 100% for canary cohort and 1–5% for background traffic.
- Diagnostic checklist:
   1. Confirm scheduler.slot_coalesce_ratio >= 0.35 for mixed workloads; lower values indicate consolidation not firing.
   2. Validate tail latency delta: p95/p99 latency should not regress by >5% on non-canary tenants.
   3. Observe speculative_kernels count; ephemeral spikes are expected but sustained high rates (>5% of total requests) require throttle.

Benchmarking suite results (summary):
- Setup: tests run on heterogeneous pool (A100-80GB and H100-80GB) with mixed load profiles derived from production traces.
- Representative results:
   - Mixed-production trace: p95 improved from 210ms -> 170ms (-19%), p99 improved 480ms -> 320ms (-33%).
   - Small chat-only: avg token cost -8%, tail unchanged within noise.
   - Long-sequence throughput: negligible change; full-batch kernels still preferred.
- Cost implication: model-nightly simulations indicate estimated GPU-hour savings of ~6–12% for workloads with >=40% small requests.

Release and rollout plan (operational steps):
1. Pre-canary validation (lab):
   - Run unit tests and scheduler integration tests from kernel-mock harness.
   - Local stress test: 2x peak synthetic traffic for 30 minutes with consolidation_enabled=true.

2. Canary phase (2 hours initial, extend to 48h):
   - Target cohort: Dedicated pools in us-west-2 running non-critical traffic by default.
   - Metrics to gate: p95 latency (service-level), kvcache.hit_rate, scheduler.credit_usage trends, error rate, GPU utilization differential.
   - Validation gates: pass if no metric breaches defined thresholds (listed below).

3. Regional rollouts: 24–72h per region, observe for systemic regressions.

4. Full global rollout: once regional rollouts are green for 7 days.

Validation thresholds (gates):
- p95 latency: no >5% regression for non-canary tenants over a 1-hour moving window.
- error rate: increase <= 0.02% absolute.
- scheduler.speculative_kernels: sustained share <= 3% of requests.
- kvcache.pagefault_rate: no >15% relative increase.

Runbook: Incidents and mitigation steps
- Symptom A: sudden p99 spike with scheduler.slot_coalesce_ratio falling to ~0.
  1. Check scheduler process health on dispatcher nodes: systemctl status adaptive-scheduler.
  2. If unstable, flip runtime-config consolidation_enabled=false for affected pools (API: POST /runtime/config with pool filter).
  3. If spike persists, rollback scheduler to fallback_adapter by setting scheduler_mode=fallback for node group; escalate to oncall.
  4. Collect traces: attach scheduler.* metrics and full-trace exports for 30 minutes prior to incident.

- Symptom B: elevated KV cache misses and cold starts after rollout
  1. Reduce speculative_hedge_threshold_ms by 50% (temporary) to reduce prefetching pressure.
  2. Increase kvcache.capacity_soft_limit by 10% via node-profile manifest.
  3. If still high, set consolidation_allowed_models to an explicit denylist containing high-kvcache models.

- Symptom C: credit exhaustion for a tenant (errors indicating admission failure)
  1. Inspect scheduler.credit_usage for tenant_id.
  2. Temporarily bump credit_window_ms for the tenant to allow refill.
  3. Investigate the tenant's traffic shape; coordinate with customer success if a production surge occurred.

Known issues observed in canary and mitigations:
- Issue 1: Transient double-charge of credit bucket on dispatcher restart (race). Mitigation: patch scheduled for 2026-03-10 (id: SCHED-1029). Temporary workaround: manually reconcile credit snapshot via /admin/scheduler/reconcile.
- Issue 2: Speculative hedging sometimes triggers when sequence length predictions are stale for long-tail models, causing unnecessary kernel warms. Mitigation: a TTL has been introduced for sequence histogram buckets (default 30s) and will be tuned; operators may lower speculative_hedge_threshold_ms.
- Issue 3: Small percentage of canary requests show increased variance in per-token latency due to coalescing fragmentation on certain tensor-core kernels. Mitigation: fallback to non-fragmented kernel variant via runtime-config for affected model variant.

Config examples (runtime-config API payloads):
- Enable consolidation for a pool:
{
  "pool_selector": "us-west-2-dedicated-small",
  "consolidation_enabled": true,
  "credit_window_ms": 1000,
  "speculative_hedge_threshold_ms": 120,
  "coalesce_allowed_models": ["redwood/llama-3b-v1", "redwood/small-chat-1"]
}

- Throttle speculative hedging globally:
{
  "speculative_hedge_throttle_percent": 20
}

Telemetry and dashboards to add/check:
- Dashboard: Scheduler Overview (new panel) - shows slot_coalesce_ratio, credit_usage heatmap by tenant, speculative_kernels timeseries, p95/p99 deltas by pool.
- Alert: scheduler.credit_saturation_high -> fires when any tenant's credit_usage > 85% for 5m.
- Alert: kvcache.miss_rate_elevated -> fires when pagefault_rate increases > 12% relative to last 1h baseline.

Ownership and escalation:
- Feature owner: Aisha Patel (Serving Runtime).
- Oncall escalation: Serving Runtime SRE rota -> if paging fails, escalate to Runtime Tech Lead (Elena Gomez).
- Patch owner for critical scheduler bugs: Marcus Chen (Kernel & Scheduling).

Testing checklist for engineers (pre-merge and release QA):
- Unit tests for credit accounting and priority synthesis.
- Integration tests validating fallback_adapter correctness under failure injection.
- Throughput/latency bench: run synthetic mixed suite and compare against baseline commit tag hash.
- Chaos tests: kill scheduler process during 10-minute steady load and verify no >10% request failure rate and fallback fires.

Post-release follow-up and telemetry audits (30/60/90 days):
- 30d: Confirm observed cost savings vs. estimate and audit any tenants excluded via denylist.
- 60d: Review kvcache behaviour and adjust TTLs for sequence histograms.
- 90d: Stability retrospective and proposal for 1.1 feature set (credit fairness refinements, cross-node consolidation).

Appendix A: Troubleshooting commands and data exports
- Export scheduler state (node): curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://dispatcher.internal/_admin/scheduler/state" > scheduler-state.json
- Reconcile credit snapshot: POST /admin/scheduler/reconcile { "node": "..." }
- Toggle consolidation from CLI: rctl runtime-config set --pool us-west-2-dedicated-small consolidation_enabled=false

Appendix B: Benchmark config snippet (YAML)
benchmark:
  name: mixed-production-sim
  duration: 3600s
  pools:
    - name: us-west-2-hetero
      nodes: 12
  trace_source: production_mixed.jl
  sampling: stratified
  metrics: [p50, p95, p99, gpu_hours, token_cost]

Appendix C: Change log highlights (implementation timeline)
- 2025-11-12: RFC accepted for predictive consolidation and credit accounting.
- 2026-01-20: Integration prototype completed; early microbenchmarks attached.
- 2026-02-18: Canary patch deployed to internal test pools.
- 2026-02-28: 1.0 release promoted to release-notes (this document).

If you are oncall and see unexpected behavior not covered above, tag #serving-runtime in Slack and include scheduler.state and a 5–10 minute trace export.
